# Visual Identity & UX Requirements Quality Checklist: SPEC 002

**Purpose**: Formal pre-`/speckit-tasks` gate — validate that the visual identity,
design-system, and UX requirements in the SPEC 002 spec are complete, clear,
consistent, and measurable before tasks are derived.
**Created**: 2026-09-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Evaluation history**:
- **2026-09-11 (pass 1, pre-implementation review)**: assessed every CHK against the current spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md and tasks.md. **16 satisfied, 6 gaps (0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 6 LOW)**. No functional scope was changed; no new tasks were required (all gaps are either non-blocking design-detail residue or already covered indirectly). Gate: **ABIERTA (open) — sin HIGH/MEDIUM pendientes.**

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the semantic color-state categories enumerated exhaustively (correcto/disponible/conectado; advertencia/atención; error/fallo/desconectado; identidad/navegación/selección/información) and is the required set of neutral roles for backgrounds, surfaces, and text specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037]
  - PASS: FR-037 enumerates the 4 semantic families verbatim plus "colores neutros para fondos, superficies y texto"; `contracts/visual-system.md` §1.1 tabulates the exact token roles (Identidad; Neutros = bg/surface/surface-raised/border/text/text-muted; 4 familias semánticas), leaving nothing open.

- [ ] CHK002 Is it specified which of the seven module headers carry a "descripción breve" and which do not, rather than deferring the decision to "cuando aporte claridad"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): FR-033 deliberately leaves this to per-module judgment ("cuando aporte claridad"); `data-model.md` §5 keeps `description` optional (`string | undefined`) and `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.2 keeps it optional at the component level. No spec artifact enumerates which of the 7 areas get one — this is left to `content/idaf.ts` (implementation), consistent with the requirement's own wording. Does not block implementation.

- [ ] CHK003 Are pass/fail criteria defined for the IDAF symbol beyond "conceptualmente asociado a redes/nodos/conectividad/IoT/diagnóstico/observabilidad", independent of evaluator opinion? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028, §SC-006]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): no SC tests the brand symbol's conceptual association in isolation. SC-006/SC-007 test the gestalt (name recognition + "network/IoT tool" perception across Login+Inicio+Topología), which indirectly exercises the symbol's contribution but never isolates it. Research D7 documents the design intent ("nodos conectados") without an independent acceptance test. Non-blocking — covered in aggregate by SC-007's rubric.

- [ ] CHK004 Is the alternate-theme expectation ("un tema alternativo … pueda añadirse más adelante sin reestructurar") backed by a traceable FR/SC, or does it exist only as an Assumption? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): confirmed — this expectation exists only in spec §Assumptions and is echoed in plan.md D6's rationale; no FR or SC anchors it. It is nonetheless satisfied structurally: `contracts/visual-system.md` §1.1 V2 requires every color declaration to pass through `tokens.css` custom properties specifically so `[data-theme="…"]` can be added later without refactor. No functional gap; a documentation-only anchor is missing.

- [x] CHK005 Are the "componentes de interfaz esenciales" that must meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast enumerated or otherwise bounded? [Clarity, Spec §SC-016]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §1.4 tabulates the exact pairs and minimum ratios (text/bg, text-muted, nav active vs. inactive, button text, state borders, focus ring), directly bounding FR-040/SC-016's "componentes esenciales".

- [ ] CHK006 Is the surface/card treatment's meaning of "unidades independientes de información" defined precisely enough to apply without sample data present? [Clarity, Spec §FR-035]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.4 repeats the same qualitative phrasing ("unidad independiente de información") without further precision. This is inherent to FR-034/FR-035's explicit prohibition on showing real or fake data in this spec — there is no sample content against which to sharpen the definition; `Surface` is deliberately data-empty. Non-blocking.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Are the qualitative adjectives "técnica, limpia, moderna y sobria" translated into any objectively checkable property, or do they remain unmeasurable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-030]
  - PASS: current FR-030 text ("técnica, limpia y sobria") is followed by explicit verifiable criteria (a)–(d) — no purely decorative imagery; animations ≤150ms, no loops; `<main>` = largest region (FR-034/SC-018); body contrast (FR-040) + line-height ≥1.4 — each mapped to SC-032/033/034/035/018.

- [x] CHK008 Is "densidad de información moderada" quantified (spacing bounds, maximum title size) so that "espacios excesivamente grandes" and "títulos sobredimensionados" are not left solely to reviewer judgment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-042, §SC (US7 item 6)]
  - PASS: FR-042(a)–(d) give explicit numeric limits (`<h1>` ≤2× body; no purposeless vertical gap >1.5× `ModuleHeader` height; decoration must not eat useful area; line-height ≥1.4 and hit-target ≥24×24px), verified by SC-034/SC-035 and `visual-criteria.test.tsx`/`tokens.test.ts`.

- [x] CHK009 Is "evolución perceptible desde prototipo navegable hacia aplicación técnica" expressed as a criterion judgeable without a side-by-side comparison to the SPEC 001 prototype? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027, §SC-007 item 5]
  - PASS: FR-027(a)–(e) and its anchor SC-036 judge the SPEC 002 result on its own terms (brand, color roles, icon family, module header, surfaces jointly present) — no comparison against a stored SPEC 001 baseline is required.

- [x] CHK010 Does the spec itself decide between wrapping and truncating a long user identifier, or does "se ajusta o trunca de forma definida" defer that choice entirely to the plan? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-045]
  - PASS: the choice is deferred to the plan as FR-050 allows, and the plan resolves it concretely — research D9 and `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.3 both specify truncation with ellipsis + full value in `title`, consistently across `data-model.md` §2.

- [x] CHK011 Is the negative requirement for the login screen ("no debe parecer un formulario administrativo tradicional ni una pantalla excesivamente decorativa") paired with a positive, checkable criterion? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029]
  - PASS: FR-029 itself supplies the positive, verifiable conditions (name+symbol, purpose text, shared control/error treatment, zero decorative imagery), anchored by SC-037 and `contracts/auth-and-session.md` §F7.

- [x] CHK012 Is "el símbolo no reemplaza al nombre" (FR-028) stated as a layout rule that can be verified (name always rendered as text alongside the mark)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §3.1 `Brand` renders the icon **and** the "IDAF" text together unconditionally, in both Login and the AppShell header — a directly verifiable layout rule.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Do the lists of shared visual aspects in FR-036 and SC-019 match? (FR-036 includes "comportamiento de navegación" and "estructura general"; SC-019 omits both.) [Conflict, Spec §FR-036, §SC-019]
  - PASS (resolved in current spec): current SC-019 text explicitly includes "comportamiento de navegación" and "estructura general" and states "la misma lista de aspectos que FR-036"; `contracts/visual-system.md` §5 confirms the 9-aspect × 7-area = 63-pair objective threshold. The discrepancy this item describes no longer exists in the spec.

- [x] CHK014 Is FR-040's "contraste suficiente" defined to be the same bar as SC-016's WCAG 2.1 AA ratios, or could the two be read as different thresholds? [Consistency, Spec §FR-040, §SC-016]
  - PASS: FR-040 states explicitly "Este es el mismo umbral que SC-016" — no ambiguity remains.

- [x] CHK015 Are the interaction states required by FR-041 (normal, seleccionado, foco de teclado, deshabilitado, error) consistent with the states referenced for the active element in FR-021 and for keyboard operability in SC-022? [Consistency, Spec §FR-041, §FR-021, §SC-022]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §4 unifies all three into one state matrix (normal/hover/seleccionado-activo/foco/deshabilitado/error) that both FR-021's active-state signals and SC-022's keyboard-focus requirement draw from.

- [x] CHK016 Is the "Sistema visual" key entity's element list (marca, roles de color, tipografía, familia iconográfica, superficies, encabezado, estados, mensajes de error) consistent with the FR set that governs each element? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities, §FR-036–§FR-042]
  - PASS: `data-model.md` §6 tabulates each "Sistema visual" aspect against its materialization and its governing FR/SC set — a complete, explicit 1:1 mapping with no orphaned aspect.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK017 Does SC-013 specify the evaluator sample (count and selection of "usuarios técnicos") required to compute the "≥ 90 %" icon-association result? [Measurability, Spec §SC-013]
  - PASS: spec §Evaluación con personas → Panel y cribado (≥5, technical network/infra profile, no design conflict) + §Rúbrica de SC-013 (mean/icon ≥0.90, floor ≥0.60, ≥80% same-family) fully specify sample and computation.

- [x] CHK018 Are SC-006 and SC-007 tied to a defined evaluation protocol (number of evaluators, what counts as a pass) rather than only the "100 %" figure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, §SC-007]
  - PASS: spec §Evaluación con personas gives literal questions, panel screening, and dedicated rubrics for both criteria with an explicit pass rule.

- [ ] CHK019 Can "el área principal de contenido … es la región de mayor superficie" be objectively verified, and is the comparison basis (viewport area, at which width) stated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-018, §FR-034]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking — same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK004): the measurement method is delegated to `structure-consistency.spec.ts` without an explicit viewport width or tolerance stated in the spec. The assertion ("main is the largest region" via bounding-box area) is close to self-evident given the AppShell's fixed 4-zone grid; the missing explicit viewport/tolerance is cosmetic, not load-bearing.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for how the content area behaves when future module content would exceed the visible area (scroll vs. clip), given FR-034 reserves it for tables/metrics/topologies? [Coverage, Spec §FR-034]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking — deliberately deferred): FR-034 explicitly states this spec "NO DEBE implementar ni simular esos contenidos", so there is no real or fake content that could overflow in SPEC 002. Overflow behavior (scroll vs. clip) is left for the future spec that actually introduces operational content. Not a defect of this spec.

- [ ] CHK021 Is the ≥ 200-character error-message behavior specified consistently between FR-047 (unquantified "no se superpone / no inutiliza") and SC-020 (quantified), including where such a message may appear (login only or any view)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-047, §SC-020]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): FR-047 is worded generically ("la vista"), not restricted to Login, and SC-020 quantifies the ≥200-char case without narrowing scope either. However `quickstart.md` E12.2 and `tasks.md` T072/T076 exercise and harden only the Login error surface; the section-error view (`RouteError`) is not explicitly walked through the same ≥200-char check even though FR-054 lists its actions among the keyboard-operable set. The requirement itself is consistent; only the test-coverage breadth for non-Login error surfaces is thin.

- [x] CHK022 Is "identidad sin color" coverage (semantic states and active module remain distinguishable) stated as applying to every color-carrying visual signal, or only to a named subset? [Coverage, Spec §FR-039, §SC-015]
  - PASS: FR-039 is a blanket rule ("cada estado DEBE ir accompanied de otra señal"), not scoped to a subset; SC-015 is its testable instance over the complete set of color-carrying signals this spec actually defines (semantic states + active nav) — there is no other color-only signal left unaddressed because none exists in scope.
